item.title: Attention-based MIA and target label k-anonymity defence
item.description: AMIA is a new attention-based MIA tailored for tabular foudnation models that exploits attention dynamics across layers and heads to infer membership information from context set. Rather than relying on shadow models or auxiliary population data, the attack requires only access to the model. The k-anonymity-based defence targets high-risk queries, achieving a drastic reduction in attack effectiveness while preserving predictive utility.

ε-PrivateSMOTE
item.description: ε-PrivateSMOTE is a technique designed for safeguarding against re-identification and linkage attacks, particularly addressing cases with a high re-identification risk. It generates synthetic data via noise-induced interpolation with differential privacy principles to obfuscate high-risk cases. ε-PrivateSMOTE allows having new cases similar to the originals while preserving privacy and maximising predictive utility. Most importantly, ε-PrivateSMOTE is a resource efficient and less time-consuming than conventional de-identification approaches such as deep learning and differential privacy-based solutions.

item.title: A Three-Way Knot: Privacy, Fairness, and Predictive Performance Dynamics
Hands-on data de-identification
item.description:
Statistical Disclosure Control seeks to reduce the risk of confidential information disclosure by de-identifying them. Such de-identification is guaranteed through privacy-preserving techniques (PPTs). However, de-identified data usually results in loss of information, with a possible impact on data analysis precision and model predictive performance. This course covers the de-identification process which aims to protect the individual’s privacy while maintaining the interpretability of the data (i.e., its usefulness). The program includes:

  • Introduction to Python
  • Introduction to data privacy
  • Predictive modeling
  • Privacy-preserving techniques
  • Training
  • Current directions on data privacy
